html:
In April 1965 young officers in Santo Domingo rose to restore Juan Bosch, the writer and elected president who had been overthrown by a coup in 1963. Fighting broke out in the capital between the rebels and the army.

President Lyndon Johnson, fearing another Cuba, sent more than twenty thousand US troops. They separated the sides and kept the rebels, led by Colonel Francisco Caamano, from winning. An inter-American force followed.

Elections in 1966 brought Joaquin Balaguer, Trujillo's former aide, to power. The intervention was widely condemned in Latin America and showed how far the United States would go in its region during the Cold War.
